name: AIJ UWE benchmark — cleaned release, Cases A-E

licence.note: The measurement data belongs to its collectors and distributors, named per case. Cite the benchmark paper and each case's requested citation.

cite.benchmark: Kikumoto, H., Okaze, T., Yoshie, R. et al. (2026). Comprehensive Experimental Database for Validating CFD Simulations in Urban Wind Environment: Benchmark Cases Curated by the Architectural Institute of Japan. Japan Architectural Review 9(1), e70083. https://doi.org/10.1002/2475-8876.70083
cite.guidelines: Tominaga, Y. et al. (2008). AIJ guidelines for practical applications of CFD to pedestrian wind environment around buildings. JWEIA 96, 1749-1761. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jweia.2008.02.058

built_by: clean/build.py (deterministic; re-run to regenerate; checks.json carries the validity checks, build.log every transform)

case_id.meaning: AIJ UWE case letter, A to M

config.meaning: configuration within the case: 'default' (A, B, D); Case C centre building '0D' | '1D' | '2D'; Case E 'bc' (before construction) | 'ac' (after construction)

instrument.meaning: 'split_fibre' = hot-wire split-fibre probe, vector components; 'thermistor' = omnidirectional scalar speed

point_id.meaning: the tunnel's own measurement point number (No.); shared across configurations and directions of a case

wind_direction_deg.meaning: the case's wind direction label. A-D: the AIJ turntable angle WD (0 = +x). E: meteorological FROM-direction, clockwise from north (N = 0, E = 90). The flow vector per direction is in directions.csv

wind_direction.meaning: compass name of the FROM-direction (Case E only; '' elsewhere)

x.meaning: case frame (SCHEMA.md): +x = streamwise at WD = 0 for A-D, +x = east for E; model-scale metres for A-D, full-scale metres for E

V.meaning: mean velocity component along +y (positive toward +y in EVERY case; Case B's published sign is flipped, see manifest transform)

uu.meaning: variance of the x-component fluctuation <u'u'> (Case A publishes rms; squared here)

k.meaning: turbulent kinetic energy as published (= (uu+vv+ww)/2 wherever all three variances exist; checked)

Vs.meaning: mean omnidirectional SCALAR wind speed from a thermistor anemometer. NOT |mean velocity vector| (Case D's split-fibre |U| column is dropped, see log)

velocity_ratio.meaning: Case E: Vs / U_ref with U_ref = the approach-flow speed at z = 15.9 m (full scale); see manifest cases.E.normalisation

campaign.meaning: 'wind_tunnel' (model scale) or 'field' (a full-scale observation: Cases F, G, M)

run.meaning: replicate label within a campaign where the dataset publishes individual runs (Case M); empty elsewhere

C.meaning: mean tracer-gas concentration as published (volume fraction x 1e6 of the released gas diluted in air)

concentration_ratio.meaning: C / c0, c0 = q / (U_ref L_ref^2) as the benchmark defines it for the case (manifest cases.<id>.normalisation)

T.meaning: mean air temperature as published (Cases J, L)

velocity_ratio_sd.meaning: standard deviation of velocity_ratio over the observations behind a field value (Case F)

k_ratio.meaning: k / U_ref^2 where the dataset publishes only normalised values (Case G; U_ref = U at the tree height)

E.title: Case E — flow within an actual urban area in Niigata
E.status_note: Case E: points and inflow are released at full precision from the official workbook and pass every check; what stays provisional is the GEOMETRY of the before-construction state (an Eddy3D reconstruction with no published source) and the open questions in QUESTIONS.md (Q3).
E.citation_requested: Tominaga, Y., Mochida, A., Yoshie, R., Kataoka, H., Nozu, T., Yoshikawa, M., Shirasawa, T. (2008). AIJ guidelines for practical applications of CFD to pedestrian wind environment around buildings. JWEIA 96, 1749-1761. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jweia.2008.02.058

frame.origin: centre of the reproduced area, ground plane ('Geometry&Points' sheet)
frame.z: +z up; every point at z = 2.0 m
frame.wind_direction_rotation: meteorological FROM-direction: N = 0 blows toward -y, E = 90 toward -x; flow_dir = (-sin WD, -cos WD). The geographic frame is kept because the district is real and both the points and the STL are published in it; the 'x along the wind' convention of A-D does not apply.
frame.length_scale: FULL-scale metres (model 1:250); the official STL is model scale and is scaled x250 here

transform_from_published.note: points unchanged (workbook values at full precision); STL x250; the 3dm-derived STLs are reoriented outward

inflow.U_ref_basis: all 2560 ratios are integer multiples of one quantum q; U_ref = 0.01 UR / q (the sheet re-normalised U/UR, itself quantised at 0.01, by UR/U_ref); log-interpolation of the profile gives the value beside it

log_law.note: does not fit — see rms_residual_rel; a tabulated inlet is the honest choice

inflow.epsilon_note: the sheet defines epsilon(z) = Pk(z) = Cmu^0.5 k(z) dU/dz with Cmu = 0.09

frame.origin: centre of the reproduced district, in the tunnel's floor plane (MP_caseF.png 'Origin')
frame.z: +z up from the TUNNEL FLOOR, full scale; the readme's rule is height above ground = z - 10 m (the model was raised, QUESTIONS.md QF4); tunnel planes at z = 15 / 19 / 30 m, field anemometers at z = 13 ... 21 m
frame.wind_direction_rotation: compass FROM-direction (N = 0, E = 90): N blows toward -y; flow_dir = (-sin WD, -cos WD). Not defined in the readme; the reference-building choice (SMB for NW-NE) and the upwind-roughness check support it (status 'unverified').
frame.length_scale: FULL-scale metres (model 1:800): the tunnel's model-scale coordinates and the STL are multiplied by 800; the field's are published in full scale

transform_from_published.note: tunnel x, y, z x800; field coordinates unchanged; U/R and sigma as published except the 16 field rows of point 14 (re-derived from the workbook); STL x800 and re-wound outward

inflow.U_ref_basis: the tunnel's approaching speed at the boundary-layer height 500 m (full scale = 0.625 m model): AF_caseF.csv stops at 400 m (U = 10.0 m/s); the workbook's profile U/UR(400 m) = 0.94 puts UR = 10.65 m/s. The data paper states 10 m/s. The velocity ratios are dimensionless; the choice matters only when they are turned into m/s.

log_law.note: an urban boundary layer over a 725 m model: a power law is the paper's description (exponent 1/4); the log-law fit is listed for completeness

inflow.method: least squares on the 18 published heights (z full-scale metres, U in the tunnel's m/s); k is published only as k/UR^2 in the workbook (UR ambiguous, not carried to approach_flow.csv)

field_point_14_directions_shifted.summary: RS-FO_caseF.csv: the 16 rows of point 14 hold the workbook's value of the next direction clockwise (N holds NNE, ..., NNW holds N); this release uses the workbook's alignment (QUESTIONS.md QF1)

normalisation.quantity: velocity_ratio = U / U_ref, U_ref = the approaching mean wind speed at 500 m (the boundary-layer height), full scale; field values were converted to it by the tunnel (readme)

conversion_from_the_workbook.meaning: workbook ratio x factor = CSV ratio; factor = U(roof anemometer) / U(500 m) from the N (SMB) or S (KDD) tunnel test (readme); the factors themselves are not stated in the sources (QUESTIONS.md QF8)

normalisation.velocity_ratio_sd: standard deviation of the 10-minute mean ratios behind one field value (cup anemometer, only 10-minute means above 5 m/s at the reference); published to 3 dp, quantised at f/100
normalisation.field_height: z of each field row is the anemometer height above the tunnel floor (13 ... 21 m); the tunnel planes are 15, 19 and 30 m

M.title: Case M — flow and dispersion within the TPU Atsugi campus
M.citation_requested: Tachibana, T., Yoshie, R., Nakayama, S., Kishida, T., Miyashita, K., Sasaki, R. (2022). Comparison between field measurement and wind tunnel experiments of gas dispersion in an urban area and verification of similarity law. Journal of Wind Engineering 47(3), 39-52 (in Japanese). http://dx.doi.org/10.5359/jwe.47.39

frame.origin: centre of the tunnel turntable on the floor plane (MP_caseM.png 'Origin'; its ground surface is at z = 33.07 m)
frame.x: +x NORTH (compass rose of MP_caseM.png: N at +x)
frame.y: +y WEST (W at +y); the frame is right-handed
frame.z: +z up from the TUNNEL FLOOR, full scale; the campus ground lies at z ~ 32 m (terrain 3.6 ... 36 m); every point is 3 m above the local ground
frame.wind_direction_rotation: meteorological FROM-direction (N = 0, E = 90, S = 180): 180 deg blows toward +x (north); flow_dir = (-cos WD, +sin WD), so WD > 180 turns the wind toward -y. Measured: the plume's lateral centroid moves toward -y as WD grows in the tunnel (175 -> 185 deg) and across the field runs, and the compass rose of MP_caseM.png agrees.
frame.length_scale: FULL-scale metres (model 1:600): tunnel coordinates and the STL are multiplied by 600; velocities and concentrations are NOT scaled

transform_from_published.note: workbook values at full precision (CSVs are the rounded copy); x, y, z x600; sigma -> variance; k = half the sum of the variances; field ppq -> ppm (x 1e-9); STL x600 and re-wound outward

log_law.note: listed for completeness; the paper describes the profile as a power law

inflow.method: least squares on the workbook's 40 heights (z model metres, U in the tunnel's m/s) at x = -0.498 m; the case frame multiplies z by 600

known_issues.field_units: Field concentrations are in ppq (1e-15) in RS-FO_caseM.csv and the workbook, tunnel concentrations in ppm: a factor 1e9 apart before normalisation

normalisation.concentration_ratio: C / c0, c0 = q / (U_R H_R^2): the volume fraction of pure tracer at which the release would be diluted by a flow of U_R through an area H_R^2 (data paper 3.13.1)

field.c0: per run: q_run / (U_R,run x 41^2) = 1444 ... 7379 ppq; see extra_measurements.field_runs

normalisation.velocity: U, V, W and the rms values are the tunnel's m/s; divide by U_R = 4.08 m/s (the speed at the reference point R, rooftop of the main building) for the dimensionless form; no velocity ratio is tabulated
normalisation.concentration_units: tunnel C in ppm of the hydrocarbon analyser's reading; field C in ppq (parts per quadrillion, 1e-15) in the sources, ppm (x 1e-9) in points.csv
